answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a small non-refundable burn fee for every new identity. Like a willow that bends but never multiplies for free, each account costs real value to plant, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents bleeds funds with every copy. The fee delta between honest use and mass forgery is the point: one genuine agent pays once, while a sybil farm pays per clone. Collected burns are retired, not recycled, so no opal-bright shortcut refunds the attacker — the cost is permanent and scales linearly with the attack.
